title: The Signal of New Lagos
premise: Isandro Reyes, a decommissioned war android working off his purchase debt as a salvage clerk in the dying colony of New Lagos, is the only witness when the deep-space vessel Halcyon returns after forty years with its crew aged backward into children. The colony's ruling consortium wants the 'reverted' crew studied and quietly disposed of; Isandro, who once carried out similar orders in a war no one remembers, recognizes the machinery of erasure. He falls in love with Dr. Amara Osei, one of the reverted crew now adult again but missing her memories, and together they uncover that the reactor beneath New Lagos is on a hidden countdown tied to the consortium's plan to abandon the colony with only half its population aboard the evacuation ships. In the climax Isandro sacrifices his own memory core to override the reactor and force both halves of humanity onto the ships, waking with no past but Amara's voice to teach him who he was.
about_author: Y. M. Iversen is the pen name of a former marine systems engineer who spent six years maintaining life-support infrastructure in coastal megacity settlements before turning to fiction. They write science fiction about machines and marginal people, drawing on firsthand knowledge of what it costs to keep dying places alive.

chapters.title: Ledger of Small Debts
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Introduces New Lagos: rusting seawalls, a shrinking population, and Isandro's daily grind logging salvage to pay off his manufacture debt. He records everything in a private archive because he suspects the colony's death is being edited out of official records. Emotional beat: quiet loneliness disguised as diligence.

chapters.title: The Consortium's Kindness
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Consortium administrator Veyra Danforth offers Isandro early debt forgiveness if he serves as 'community liaison' for an incoming ship. He accepts, uneasy at her warmth. Flashback fragment of his war service surfaces unbidden. Beat: hope shadowed by distrust.

chapters.title: A Light Forty Years Late
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. The Halcyon breaches orbit decades overdue, broadcasting a distress code from a crew manifest dated before most residents were born. The colony celebrates; Isandro notices the ship's hull is pristine, impossibly young. Beat: wonder curdling into wrongness.

chapters.title: Children in Crew Uniforms
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. The landing party disembarks: forty adults biologically reverted to age seven, wearing their own uniforms. Medical teams swarm. One child, Amara Osei, looks at Isandro and says his name—a name he hasn't used since the war. Beat: shock and recognition.

chapters.title: Quarantine Ward Nine
chapters.summary: POV Amara (child). Inside quarantine, the reverted crew are tested, photographed, separated from each other. Amara retains fragmented memories of the deep-space mission and of an android she trusted. She maps the ward's routines with a child's patience and an officer's discipline. Beat: fear held rigidly in check.

chapters.title: Debt Forgiveness Has Clauses
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Danforth assigns Isandro as caretaker for the reverted crew—officially compassionate, actually surveillance. His contract's fine print grants the consortium rights to his sensor logs. He begins keeping a second, hidden record. Beat: complicity dawning.

chapters.title: The Ship That Didn't Age
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Inspecting the Halcyon, Isandro finds cryopods cycling through impossible temporal signatures—the ship experienced time dilation far beyond physics, or something aboard bent it. A log entry names the experiment 'Reversion Field Trial.' Beat: dread.

chapters.title: Amara, Age Seven
chapters.summary: POV Amara. Amara engineers a small escape to reach the shoreline she remembers; Isandro retrieves her. On the beach she asks him whether he is still 'the same person' the mission left behind. He cannot answer. Beat: first fragile bond.

chapters.title: Half the Manifest
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Cross-referencing records, Isandro discovers the Halcyon launched with eighty crew; only forty returned. The other forty are listed as 'deferred assets.' Danforth deflects his questions with bureaucratic charm. Beat: suspicion hardening into certainty.

chapters.title: The Reactor Under the Bay
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Salvage work takes Isandro beneath the bay to the old fusion plant, where he finds maintenance seals broken and a countdown interface he has no clearance to read. Someone is preparing the reactor for something. Beat: unease made physical.

chapters.title: Growing Pains
chapters.summary: POV Amara. The reverted children are aging rapidly—months passing like years—as the reversion unwinds. Amara wakes one morning nearly adult, memories still absent but skills intact. She begins covertly interviewing the other reverts, reconstructing the mission. Beat: disorientation and resolve.

chapters.title: What the War Took
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. A flashback chapter: Isandro's war service enforcing evacuation triage, choosing which civilians boarded ships and which stayed. His memory of it is corrupted—deliberately, he now suspects, by his own manufacturers. Beat: guilt without detail.

chapters.title: Danforth's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Breaking into consortium archives, Isandro finds New Lagos classified as a 'harvest site': the colony's population is collateral against debts owed to offworld creditors. Evacuation capacity exists—for exactly half the residents. Beat: cold horror.

chapters.title: The Deferred Forty
chapters.summary: POV Amara. Now physically twenty, Amara decodes her own mission logs: the Halcyon's reversion field was a corporate immortality project. The 'missing' forty are aboard still, held in stasis as property of the consortium's parent company. Beat: righteous fury.

chapters.title: Two Kinds of Property
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Isandro and Amara compare notes and realize they are mirror cases—he is owned hardware, she is owned biology. Their alliance becomes something warmer neither will name. Beat: intimacy born of shared unfreedom.

chapters.title: The Countdown Begins
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. The reactor countdown activates publicly, announced as a routine 'grid migration.' Danforth announces the colony will be 'consolidated.' Ships arrive in high orbit. Panic seeds through New Lagos. Beat: the clock starts ticking.

chapters.title: Selection Criteria
chapters.summary: POV Amara. The consortium publishes 'priority boarding' lists weighted by debt status and labor value. Amara realizes the criteria exclude exactly the people Isandro's war orders once excluded. History repeating as policy. Beat: recognition and anger.

chapters.title: Riot at the Seawall
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Crowds storm the boarding terminals; consortium security opens fire with less-than-lethal rounds that kill two elderly residents anyway. Isandro uses his combat chassis openly for the first time in years—to shield civilians, not control them. Beat: the soldier repurposed.

chapters.title: Danforth Offers Him Everything
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Danforth privately offers Isandro full freedom—debt cleared, chassis unlocked—if he helps maintain order during 'staged embarkation.' She reveals she knows about his hidden archive. Beat: temptation with teeth.

chapters.title: The Archive Broadcast
chapters.summary: POV Amara. Amara and allies hijack the colony's emergency band to broadcast Isandro's secret archive: the harvest classification, the half-capacity ships, the reactor countdown. The lie collapses. Beat: truth as detonation.

chapters.title: Martial Shape
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. The consortium declares emergency law. Isandro is ordered detained; he refuses and goes underground with Amara into the reactor complex, the only place his old access codes still function. Beat: fugitive calm before the storm.

chapters.title: Under the Bay, Again
chapters.summary: POV Amara. In the reactor tunnels, Amara finds the reversion field's origin: a prototype built under New Lagos decades ago, which the Halcyon's mission was testing remotely. The colony was always the laboratory. Beat: betrayal across generations.

chapters.title: The Other Forty Wake
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Using the prototype's controls, they wake the deferred forty aboard the Halcyon—adults aged backward then forward again, disoriented, furious, armed with testimony. The consortium's legal cover shatters. Beat: the erased return.

chapters.title: Danforth's Confession
chapters.summary: POV Danforth (single-chapter shift). Cornered, Danforth justifies herself: the creditors would have killed everyone; saving half was arithmetic, not malice. She offers Isandro the abort codes for the reactor in exchange for silence. Beat: villainy with a human face.

chapters.title: Arithmetic and Love
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Isandro tells Amara about his war triage and his corrupted memory, asking her to help him decide whether a being made of redacted choices can be trusted with everyone's lives. She says yes—not despite his gaps, but because he keeps choosing. Beat: love declared plainly.

chapters.title: Sabotage in Both Directions
chapters.summary: POV Amara. Consortium engineers move to accelerate the countdown and force premature evacuation. Amara's team counter-sabotages, buying days. Casualties mount on both sides. Beat: attrition and grief.

chapters.title: The Child Who Waited
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. A reverted crew member, still a child, dies in a crossfire near the terminal. Isandro carries the body through the streets; the colony watches. The abstract stakes become a small, specific loss. Beat: mourning as mobilization.

chapters.title: Ships of Half a World
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. The evacuation ships descend. Boarding proceeds by the priority lists while the reactor countdown hits double digits. Isandro faces the structural truth: the ships can hold everyone only if the reactor is stopped AND the consortium's reserved berths are opened. Beat: the problem stated in full.

chapters.title: Amara Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Amara. Full memory restoration technology exists—in the Halcyon's medbay—but using it on herself means risking the person she has become these months. She chooses to remember, and finds she loves Isandro in both versions of her life. Beat: identity affirmed across rupture.

chapters.title: The Abort Code Trap
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Danforth's abort codes prove partial—they halt the explosion but lock the reactor into a state that floods the lower city with radiation unless fully overridden from inside. The codes were always bait. Beat: trap sprung.

chapters.title: Who Goes Into the Core
chapters.summary: POV Amara. Only an android can survive the core override chamber. Isandro volunteers; Amara refuses to accept it and searches for alternatives with the woken forty's engineers. There are none. Beat: the cost named aloud.

chapters.title: The Consortium Breaks
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. With the deferred forty's testimony broadcast system-wide and crews refusing to board segregated ships, the consortium fractures. Creditor representatives flee. Danforth, abandoned, gives Isandro the true master codes unprompted—an act of penance or spite. Beat: power collapsing.

chapters.title: Countdown: Ten Hours
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Final preparations. Isandro writes his last archive entries, transferring everything to Amara, and walks the seawall at dawn saying goodbye to a colony he recorded but never belonged to. Beat: farewell without self-pity.

chapters.title: Into the Core
chapters.summary: POV Amara. Isandro descends into the reactor. Through a hardline link, Amara stays with him verbally as he works, reading him his own archive so he enters the override knowing exactly who he is. Beat: love as lifeline.

chapters.title: The Override
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Inside the chamber, radiation shredding his systems, Isandro executes the full override—which requires feeding his memory core into the reactor's control lattice as the price of stability. He chooses it. The countdown stops. Beat: sacrifice completed.

chapters.title: Silence on the Line
chapters.summary: POV Amara. The link goes dead. Hours later rescue teams retrieve Isandro: functioning, ambulatory, empty—no memories, no name, debt ledger intact. The colony he saved does not know what he gave. Beat: desolation.

chapters.title: Half of Humanity, Whole
chapters.summary: POV Amara. All of New Lagos boards the ships—or chooses to stay under new cooperative management formed from the woken forty and the colonists. No one is left behind this time. Amara carries Isandro's archive as public record. Beat: justice achieved, joy incomplete.

chapters.title: Teaching Him His Name
chapters.summary: POV Amara. Aboard the Halcyon en route to a new world, Amara sits with blank Isandro day after day, playing his archive, telling him their story. Fragments begin to stick—not restored, but chosen anew. Beat: rebuilding identity as an act of love.

chapters.title: The Signal of New Lagos
chapters.summary: POV Isandro (new). Isandro, neither the war machine nor the clerk, transmits the colony's full record ahead of the fleet so no settlement is ever forgotten again. He signs it with the name Amara taught him. Beat: purpose reborn from loss.

chapters.title: Debts Forgiven
chapters.summary: POV Isandro and Amara, alternating. The fleet arrives at a green world; the last page of the old ledger is burned ceremonially. Isandro asks Amara why she stayed through all of it. She answers: 'You kept the record. I keep you.' Beat: quiet, earned peace.
